Today, both communities celebrate Vaisakhi as a time of harvest and renewal.

long_description:
**Can Philosophy Prescribe Anything?**

There are many philosophies that aim to prescribe instead of purely describe behavior. Stoicism pursues virtue. Epicureanism seeks tranquility. Utilitarianism maximizes wellbeing. Kant says to act on principles you could will universally. Each prescribes, and each prescription rests on a claim about what matters. But do any of these philosophies have the standing to prescribe at all? As Hume noted, you can't get an "ought" from an "is" alone. Every prescriptive argument needs a normative premise, and where those premises come from is unclear. It’s also difficult for prescriptive philosophies to be fully non-contradictory. For example, some Epicureans would refuse to enter Robert Nozick's hypothetical experience machine, a device that permanently gives you any experience you want, indistinguishable from reality. But this
would seem to be contradictory with the Epicurean goal of maximizing the feeling of tranquility. Can any prescriptive philosophy be fully consistent with one’s intuition? And what gives intuition the ultimate authority? Can any prescriptive philosophy survive the is-ought problem, or are they all just confident assertions of preference? Even more broadly, when can we ever say “should”, and does any of this matter for how we actually live?

No reservations needed just bring a desire to have some fun, flat soled shoes or sneakers and a hat. We hope you enjoy the lesson so much that you’ll return again and maybe join as a member (annual dues are great value for money).

Email [berkeleylawnbowling@gmail.com](mailto:berkeleylawnbowling@gmail.com) or check the [BLBC website](https://berkeleylawnbowling.org/free-lessons/) for more information.

long_description:
We invite you for an early summer lunch and talk by Fish Stark, Executive Director of the American Humanist Association, at the India Pavilion as he discusses how the AHA is fighting the unprecedented surge of religious extremism (bolstered by recent pro-religious US government actions), along with our allies in the secular and religious communities.

His talk is titled "How Humanists are Fighting Religious Extremism and Christian Nationalism".

"The religious right is waging the most aggressive assault on secular values in a generation — defunding public schools, pushing religion into government, and attacking empathy itself as a weakness and a sin. But the picture isn't all bleak. Efforts to force the Bible into public school classrooms are being defeated in court. The AHA just won a major federal case in Florida.

The Congressional Freethought Caucus we helped start is now larger than the Freedom Caucus. And from Minneapolis to Biloxi, humanists are showing what is possible when we show up for our communities. AHA Executive Director Fish Stark will break down the threats the AHA's legal and policy teams are tracking right now, where the most serious attacks on the First Amendment are coming from, and what humanists can do to fight back — in the courts, in Congress, in the culture, and in our communities."

**Fish Stark** is Executive Director of the AHA. As organizer, educator, social entrepreneur, and lifelong humanist, he has spent his career turning big ideas into bold action in service of belonging, flourishing, and social justice for all people.

**THE RESTAURANT**
The India Pavillion in Central Square Cambridge (vegetarian options\*). It is $17 per person for all you care to eat, not including drinks; bring cash or check made to GBHumanists, please).
Parking in Cambridge is free on Sundays in metered and some non-metered spots, and several garages and lots in Central Square including several just steps away on Green Street. MBTA red line Central Square stat

organizer: San Francisco Yoga + Karate + Writing Meetup Group
long_description:
**Mysore Style Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga**
Mysore Style Ashtanga Vinyasa Yoga is named after the city in South India; Mysore where this transformative practice originated from the co-founders Krishnamacharya & K. Pattabhi Jois nearly 90 years ago. Mysore style means you work at your own pace while the teacher provides tailored instruction from giving postures, asking questions, & giving hands-on adjustments when necessary. The beauty of Mysore is you don’t need to keep up with the teacher or other students in the room since it is an individual practice similar to an individual playing a song on a guitar, doing a dance or doing a kata in martial arts in a customized way. Since the same postures are repeated each time you can memorize the sequence giving you practice to take home with you or wherever you roam on Mother Earth.
Bio:
Shane has had daily Mysore yoga practice for nearly 20 years. He practiced and studied with/ Master teachers in North America & India including Richard Freeman, Mary Taylor, Rolf Naujokat, & Marci Naujokat. Shane has had a daily yoga practice since 2003 & has been teaching yoga since 2004.

A Truly Invigorating Social Event,

Where people - often strangers - meet and tell stories.
Nobody knows what story they are going to tell.

It's time to truly connect again in the way that only sitting in real life, with real people, telling real-life stories can.

Storytelling is the capability we have used to connect with one another and create the modern world. And yet, especially on social media, we have reduced storytelling to story-selling and mostly share opinions rather than real-life experiences.

Our events are simple, timed, unprepared story prompts that help everyone who listens connect to our unique and yet relatable experiences. Often, the stories told are intensely funny, sometimes emotional, but always interesting.

I call them games rather than exercises because they are fun and often frivolous, but there's no competition and no one loses - except those who don't attend! 😀

[No Stress Hydro-Gardens](https://maps.app.goo.gl/P5tUAQkbz2Sd8Hk87)

We will start with a couple of simple story rounds for the storytellers. The first is almost always 'The Story of your name' because everyone is **the** world's expert in living their life with their name.

long_description:
**Spirituality in Nature Hike: Exploring the Power of Order**

Join us for a reflective walk in nature as we explore the spiritual power of Order. In Unity teachings, Order is our innate ability to organize, balance, sequence, and adjust our lives according to Divine Ideas and Principles.

As we walk, we'll observe the natural patterns, rhythms, and interconnected systems of the earth, discovering how creation expresses a deeper intelligence and harmony.
Through guided reflection and conversation, we'll consider how Divine Order is at work within us and around us—helping us align our thoughts, choices, and actions with higher wisdom. Together, we'll open ourselves to the flow of life, trusting the unfolding sequence of growth, change, and renewal that is present in every season of nature and every stage of our spiritual journey.

This will be a moderate-paced hike with some possible rough terrain and gentle hills. Please wear sturdy footwear and bring a water bottle. You might want to bring a small journal to capture any thoughts from the afternoon.

long_description:
ASRG-D Meetup: Building & Securing the Modern Vehicle

Join us at SAE International on June 1st for an evening dedicated to the core pillars of automotive cybersecurity. This session is designed to give you an inside look at how we design secure vehicles and protect the data moving inside them.

What’s on the Agenda?

Architecture-Centric Cybersecurity & TARA:

**Rex Struble (VxLabs)** kicks things off by explaining how to build security into a vehicle's "blueprint" from day one. He’ll explore TARA (Threat Analysis and Risk Assessment), showing how we identify and manage risks in the early design phase.
Securing the Data Highway (DDS): After a quick pizza break,

**Ron Oliver (RTI)** will dive into DDS (Data Distribution Service). You’ll learn how this technology allows vehicle systems to share data instantly and, more importantly, how we keep those data streams locked down against cyber threats.

The Schedule:

5:30 PM: Doors open for Networking
6:00 PM: Architecture & TARA Deep-Dive (Rex Struble from VxLabs)
6:30 PM: Pizza Break (Sponsored by VxLabs)
6:40 PM: DDS & Data Security (Ron Oliver from RTI)
7:10 PM: Open Q&A and Final Networking

long_description:
Looking for a dedicated hour to finally read that book, meet new people, and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere of **Chinatown LA**? Our Silent Book Club is the perfect low-pressure gathering for **friendly, likeminded readers**.

The structure is simple and designed for maximum reading time: we meet up, say a quick hello to our fellow book-lovers, and then settle in for a full hour of **uninterrupted, quiet reading**. It’s a wonderful way to connect with your community without the pressure of small talk.

**CLASS DESCRPTION:**
Join us for our weekly Indian dance class and step into the diverse, enchanting world of Indian dance and cinema. In this class, you will learn fun, feel-good choreographies to hit songs from Bollywood, and other regional film industries such as Tamil, Telugu, and Malayalam.

The choreographies will be a lively blend of folk (Kuthu, Bhangra, Garba), western, and semi-classical dance styles, celebrating the rich variety of Indian movement and expression. One of the most beautiful aspects of Indian “filmy” dance is its ability to transcend boundaries, with no strict rules or restrictions, making it accessible and enjoyable for everyone.

long_description:
**Welcome to Bhakti Night** \- an evening dedicated to the wisdom and practice of *bhakti-yoga*.

The evening begins with a soul-stirring *kirtan*, a musical form of meditation, where the air will resonate with melodious chants and the rhythmic beats of traditional instruments. As the sweet sound vibrations fill the room, you'll find your heart opening up, and any stress or worries gently dissipate, replaced by a profound sense of peace and contentment. The *kirtan* is followed by a talk on teachings from the ancient yoga tradition which is always thought provoking and even entertaining!

As the night draws to a close, we'll conclude with a delightful vegetarian dinner. Savor the sanctified dishes, lovingly prepared with devotion, and experience how food can be an offering of love and nourishment for the soul.

Whether you are a seasoned practitioner or a curious newcomer, this program promises an evening filled with spiritual bliss and inner harmony. We look forward to sharing this wonderful journey of devotion with you!

organizer: Fish and Bear Network - Storytelling games night
long_description:
The most enjoyable way to meet new people. Mostly listening, you'll hear our similarities and our uniqueness. Both peaceful & invigorating.

**[We post our events on multiple platforms. Please RSVP at [fishandbear.net](http://fishandbear.net/) if you'd prefer to pay on the night.]([https://fishandbear.net](https://fishandbear.net/))**

A Truly Invigorating Social Event,
Where people - often strangers - meet and tell stories.
Nobody knows what story they are going to tell.

We’re bringing back real human connection through spontaneous, unscripted storytelling. No performances, no opinions, no story-selling — just real people sharing real experiences.

Storytelling is the capability we have used to connect with one another and create the modern world. And yet, especially on social media, we have reduced storytelling to story-selling and mostly share opinions rather than real-life experiences.

Our events feature simple, timed story prompts that help everyone who listens connect with our unique yet relatable experiences. Often, the stories told are intensely funny, sometimes emotional, but always interesting.

I call them games rather than exercises because they are fun and often frivolous, but there's no competition and no one loses - except those who don't attend! 😀

**Arrive before the start.**
[Parlor Room](https://maps.app.goo.gl/bRZCziBEiJKrjiKo6) (Within the Church of the Valley complex)
We have a sweet room and a lovely courtyard for our use, so please arrive on time so that we can start promptly at 7 pm. We shut the gates once we have started.

**Let the Games begin.**
We will start with a couple of simple story rounds for the storytellers. The first is almost always 'The Story of your name' because everyone is **the** world's expert in living their life with their name.

**Break!**
We host these events to encourage connection and community, so this break is there to keep it light and cheerful. So stretch, chat, and find the restroom across the courtyard. 🚽!

In 1948, Clément Mathieu, an unemployed music teacher, takes a job as a supervisor at a boarding school for troubled boys. Disturbed by the headmaster’s harsh discipline, he introduces the students to music and choral singing. Through this, Mathieu gradually transforms their daily lives.

A major box office success, *Les Choristes* became one of the most beloved films in modern French cinema, capturing audiences in France and around the world. The movie earned international recognition, including nominations at the Academy Awards and Golden Globe Awards. long_description:
Welcome!!

Meditation + Tea is a monthly gathering, for women of color to meditate and converse about cultivating more joy in our lives over a cup of delicious herbal tea.

This relaxed and informal gathering begins with a guided meditation designed to relieve stress, build community, and create space to unwind the narratives that block the flow of joy.
We will deepen the connection between mind, body, and heart through meditation, followed by conversation about living with meaningful joy over a cup of delicious herbal tea. (Our blends are cultivated and created by Ursula and Stephanie and shared for your enjoyment)

Our June gathering will be an evening of soulful movement meditation designed to help you reconnect with your body, breath, and inner rhythm.

long_description:
Our NEIGHBORHOOD GEMS series features emblematic meals from around the world. This series shines a light on local restaurants and is designed to bring together inquisitive foodies and dishes that are unique and oh so worth a trip on roads less traveled!

Join us for authentic Hunan & Szechuan dishes at ***Chef Tan***!

**From Washington Post**

Chef Tan invites diners to experience the tongue-tingling pleasures of one of China’s great cuisines in an understated Vienna strip mall.

When Chef Tan opened in Vienna last July, the restaurant had no website and initially offered neither takeout nor delivery. Albert Yang, the restaurant’s regional manager, believed that diners should experience Hunan cooking at its freshest and most vibrant. “If you pack it to deliver, the color, the oil, the meat will change,” he says. This was a sacrifice he wasn’t willing to make, even if it meant losing business.

Because of the low-key opening, I didn’t get wind of Chef Tan until February. Others had clearly beaten me to the punch. On my first visit, all but the large banquet tables in the handsome, wood-paneled dining room were occupied by chattering friends. Soon, my own table filled. Thinly sliced pork belly buried under waxy, modestly spicy green peppers. Morsels of chicken sweetly perfumed with ginger and surrounded by chopped red chiles packing merciless, browbeating heat. Tender slivers of lamb, ornamented with grassy cilantro and mild, neatly diced red peppers.

As I inhaled steam abundant with chopped chiles, pungent fermented peppers and dark, sharp vinegar, I understood Yang’s stubbornness. This was not food destined for a takeout container. I floated back to the parking lot, in awe of the mastery quietly playing out between a paint supply store and a beer and wine shop in this Northern Virginia strip mall.

long_description:
We will be catching the Claude and OpenClaw wave.

Over the holidays I was pretty close to relaunching this meetup- and then I read the following post by Andrej Karpathy (OpenAI, Tesla) - which exactly summed up the way I was feeling...

"I've never felt this much behind as a programmer. The profession is being dramatically refactored as the bits contributed by the programmer are increasingly sparse and between. I have a sense that I could be 10X more powerful if I just properly string together what has become available over the last \~year and a failure to claim the boost feels decidedly like skill issue. There's a new programmable layer of abstraction to master (in addition to the usual layers below) involving agents, subagents, their prompts, contexts, memory, modes, permissions, tools, plugins, skills, hooks, MCP, LSP, slash commands, workflows, IDE integrations, and a need to build an all-encompassing mental model for strengths and pitfalls of fundamentally stochastic, fallible, unintelligible and changing entities suddenly intermingled with what used to be good old fashioned engineering. Clearly some powerful alien tool was handed around except it comes with no manual and everyone has to figure out how to hold it and operate it, while the resulting magnitude 9 earthquake is rocking the profession. Roll up your sleeves to not fall behind." - A (Original X post here: [Karpathy](https://x.com/karpathy/status/2004607146781278521?ref_src=twsrc%5Egoogle%7Ctwcamp%5Eserp%7Ctwgr%5Etweet))

We started back in 2017- you can find about 100 hours of presentation materials in our repo:
[Metrowest Boston Developers Machine Learning Group · GitHub](https://github.com/MetrowestBostonDevelopersMLGroup)

long_description:
Hesse's famous and influential novel, *Siddartha*, is perhaps the most important and compelling moral allegory our troubled century has produced. Integrating Eastern and Western spiritual traditions with psychoanalysis and philosophy, this strangely simple tale, written with a deep and moving empathy for humanity, has touched the lives of millions since its original publication in 1922. Set in India, Siddhartha is the story of a young Brahmin's search for ultimate reality after meeting with the Buddha. His quest takes him from a life of decadence to asceticism, through the illusory joys of sensual love with a beautiful courtesan, and of wealth and fame, to the painful struggles with his son and the ultimate wisdom of renunciation. This new translation by award-winning translator Joachim Neugroschel includes an introduction by Hesse biographer Ralph Freedman.

This meeting will take place in person in the Rice Village area of Houston Texas. Once you RSVP and your spot is confirmed, we will send directions to the meeting room.

*Seating for the event is limited, and priority is given to regularly attending members. If no spots are available, we encourage you to join the waitlist. We will make every effort to accommodate additional attendees should space permit.*

long_description:
Join YNP Connect for the next edition of our Language Lounge, this time we are exploring the Igbo language and culture in a relaxed, welcoming environment.

The YNP Language Lounge is designed as an interactive space where Nigerian professionals and friends can learn, practice, and reconnect with Nigerian languages, no pressure, just participation.

• Interactive activities and group participation
• A relaxed, social atmosphere to connect with others

Come as you are. Make mistakes. Learn. Laugh. Connect.

long_description:
I know many people have never had the pleasure of eating Afghan food. So let's go to Kabul Kabob and enjoy some amazing authentic Afghan food.

Trust me you will love the Afghan food at Kabul Kabob and become a more sophisticated foodie.

Afghan food is a diverse, aromatic blend of Central Asian, Persian, and South Asian influences, characterized by a refined balance of spices—not heat—and fresh ingredients. Rice is a staple, often featured in pilafs with lamb or beef, alongside fresh naan, yogurt, and fruits. It is flavorful and hearty, using mild spices like coriander, cumin, and turmeric.

**Key Characteristics of Afghan Cuisine**

* **The National Dish:** *[Kabuli Pulao](https://www.google.com/search?client=firefox-b-1-d&q=Kabuli+Pulao&mstk=AUtExfA1SQ295jfEAT0jD8TfLDBm54jJmdXizpjFyywrl-O5aHLovQjifv7Fd2a1d1WJKRKw0Bj1aQQfiafxhIqkqNS9nbJsxRu9gwN9QBrPxqoLOi8j6Ntyg9L8ACswnzSDi5U&csui=3&ved=2ahUKEwisrviM9JqUAxWa2BoGHQIONCQQgK4QegYIAQgAEA0)* is a famous rice dish made with lamb or beef, topped with carrots and raisins.
* **Mild Spices:** Afghan cuisine often uses aromatic, not fiery spices, such as *char masala* (a blend similar to Indian masala but without chili).
* **Main Ingredients:** Lamb, chicken, and beef are staples, along with hearty vegetables like spinach, eggplant, and potatoes.
* **Dairy & Herbs:** Fresh yogurt is used as a topping, dressing, or drink (called *[Shomleh](https://www.google.com/search?client=firefox-b-1-d&q=Shomleh&mstk=AUtExfA1SQ295jfEAT0jD8TfLDBm54jJmdXizpjFyywrl-O5aHLovQjifv7Fd2a1d1WJKRKw0Bj1aQQfiafxhIqkqNS9nbJsxRu9gwN9QBrPxqoLOi8j6Ntyg9L8ACswnzSDi5U&csui=3&ved=2ahUKEwisrviM9JqUAxWa2BoGHQIONCQQgK4QegYIAQgCEAI)*). Fresh cilantro, mint, and parsley are commonly used.
* **Essential Side Items:** Various types of naan (flatbread) accompany nearly every meal.

long_description:
Hey Poetry Lovers!

This group is on a roll. Here’s the gist:

We meet at the **Capital One Café in Chinatown** from **12pm - 2pm** every other week.

For enrichment, we start by reading and reflecting on a **“published poem”**, suggested by someone in the group. No advance preparation is necessary. But feel free to check out some of the poems we’ve read [here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/e/2PACX-1vSyE_wCLQCPHRrKmN5F9tOIeeRQUZESxjRXGVBoCF2uU8Gm0_d0uECiCBCQXEy6ksxfsBOhtRIOpW3T/pubhtml?gid=0&single=true&widget=true&headers=false%22%3E%3C/iframe%3E). Or submit suggestions for future meetings [here](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSexGc2Z2Kp6bZW0D3_hfJ7NUUkfNHf7TXX-43FglCeBd9EF2Q/viewform?usp=send_form).

Next, we **share our work and offer feedback**. Depending on attendance, everyone gets \~10 minutes to use as they like. (No need to share, though; you’re welcome to come even if you prefer just to listen.)

We maintain a **Discord server** to help share our work and communicate outside our bi-weekly meet-ups. If you haven’t used Discord before, take a moment to download it and create an account before arriving. When we meet you on Saturday, we will add you to our server, the “DC Poetry Workshop”, and can help you navigate the app if you have questions.

Finally, if you plan on sharing a poem, consider how you will do so. Some options include:

* Print 5-10 copies to distribute in person
* Take and share screenshots in the Discord chat.
* Copy the poem into a google doc, change sharing settings to “anyone with link”, and copy the google doc link into the Discord chat.

Most importantly, we’re excited to meet you!

Catch you on Saturday,

Diego / Ian / Cayden / Nate / Otasha / Lia / An

long_description:
**WHAT TO EXPECT**
Kirtan Soulfest is simply a transcendental party guaranteed to uplift you mentally, physically, and emotionally. The sacred mantras chanted in a call-and-response manner is the prescribed method given in the Vedas to link the inner divinity within all of us. This link connects us to the real happiness, peace and love we are all searching for.
Come with an open heart, dance and leave with an overflow of LOVE!

**WHAT IS MANTRA MEDITATION?**
Mantra Meditation is a type of Sound Bath and Yoga which is an immersive experience combining powerful soundwaves and group singing/chanting to help individuals better connect with their inner selves. Yoga means to unite, Mantra Meditation will help unite your mind to your body and soul.
The sounds and singing during a Mantra Meditation session are an invitation to journey into a deeper state of consciousness as an opportunity to gain perspective on what's going on within you. The goal of the experience is to invite deep relaxation, restoration and explore self-inquiry and self-discovery.

**WHO IS THIS FOR?**
Mantra Meditation is a growing movement in North America derived from ancient Vedic traditions and is applicable to everyone. However, some examples of individuals who might greatly benefit from Mantra Meditation are:

* If you want to relax, refresh and nourish yourself
* Stress, anxiety, or overwhelm dominate your life
* You're challenged by illness
* Grieving the loss of someone or even the past
* You're seeking a breakthrough in understanding your higher purpose
* You're looking to deepen your healing wisdom and spiritual connection
* You're wanting to connect with a community of compassionate, inclusive and supportive beings alike

Mantra meditation has different effects on everyone and is a deeply personal interaction with the sound vibrations.

Guru Pooja is a certain science of using chants and offerings to manifest a powerful experience in your living space. This particular Guru Pooja is known as Shodashopachara, which refers to sixteen ways of welcoming a Guru. Guru Pooja is offered to a lamp as a symbol of all the great masters, regardless of what culture or religion they belong to.

Guru Pooja Training is a two-day program conducted by an Ishanga (instructor) trained by Sadhguru.

**Program Guidelines & Session Information:**

* ***Attendance at all sessions is mandatory to complete the program. If you miss one session, your admission into the class will be at the discretion of the organizers.***
* Please do not book flights departing before 3 hours from the closing time on the last day of the program to allow yourself enough time to get to the airport.
* **Note**: There is an optional Guru Pooja practice correction session offered on Monday morning after the program from 7-9am, further details will be provided during the program.
* Stay will not be possible before, during or after the program dates. However, meals will be provided during the program and doctor-prescribed dietary restrictions will be accommodated.
* Participants will receive corrections on the words of the Guru Pooja chant via video call 2-4 weeks before the program. Please memorize the chant to the best of your ability. You can access the Guru Pooja chant on the Sadhguru App and a separate link to the chant and words will be provided to you upon registration.

Saturday, June 6th, 8:00 AM - 6:30 PM
Sunday, June 7th, 8:00 AM - 6:30 PM

Let’s head to upper Northwest DC for an Indian dinner at Masala Art in Tenleytown, a long-running neighborhood favorite known for refined North Indian cuisine and regional specialties. The restaurant was founded by chef Surinder Singh, formerly of Heritage India, and continues to maintain a strong reputation for consistent execution and depth of flavor.

**FOOD**: Masala Art focuses on North Indian cuisine with a mix of classic curries, tandoori dishes, and harder-to-find regional specialties. Recent diners frequently highlight the Railway Lamb Curry, lamb korma dishes, garlic naan, and vegetarian items such as baingan bharta and okra preparations. Tandoori items and biryanis are also consistently well reviewed, with many diners noting balanced spice levels and strong flavor without excessive heaviness.

The menu supports a wide range of preferences, including vegetarian-friendly selections and several richer meat-based dishes. Expect traditional Indian desserts and a full bar with wine, cocktails, and beer available.

Most members should expect total spend to land roughly in the 40 to 70 dollar range, depending on ordering style & beverage participation.

long_description:
Join us at the weekly Kirtan and in celebrating all current month's birthdays!

Welcome, please join our community for call and response Kirtan & Chai, chanting mantras and devotional songs.

Kirtan is immediately after the weekly SoundBath & Prana Lifeforce Healing (430pm-530pm). It is for everyone, participate or just enjoy the energy / rhythms.

Welcome to bring, but not required, a vegan/vegetarian dish to share for social after the Kirtan.

What is Kirtan:
Kirtan is the Yoga of Devotion (Bhakti Yoga). Derived from a Sanskrit root meaning to call, recite, praise, or glorify, put simply, kirtan is the act of praising and glorifying the Divine.

Why Kirtan:
Chanting Kirtan is a devotional practice that helps to uplift the mind, open the heart and bring inner peace. It is the fastest, easiest and most joyful way to achieve peace of mind. The mantras are mystical universal sounds that resonate with our chakras and remove negative energies. So, it is important that we chant so that we can benefit from this powerful healing energy.

Curious how to start learning something? Want to chat with someone of another discipline? Need a place to work on a project and share it with others? ISG is a social, game development focused work group that encourages people of all skill levels and disciplines to come together and collaborate for the benefit of all.

**Bring your laptop** and any software you will need to work on your game/art/music.

How it Works:

• Show up, introduce yourself, let everyone know what you hope to accomplish

• Ask for help with anything, get to know others, share your projects, or enjoy the company of others as you work!

• Share your highs and lows, high fives all around

***

How to find us:
It can be kind of hard to find us! We are on the 4th floor of the Armory building. Follow the signs to the restrooms, and nearby you'll find the stairs and the elevator. Take one of those to the fourth floor and look for the Seattle Indies banner.

***

Accessibility information:
There is paid street parking all around the neighborhood. There are paid parking garages at 516 Harrison St, 650 3rd Ave N, and at the corner of 5th Ave N and Harrison St. The Seattle Center has nearby bus stops serviced by the 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 13, 15, 17, 18, 19, 24, 32, 33, D Line, and the monorail. The venue is listed as wheelchair accessible. The Seattle Center has additional accessibility information available on their website here: http://www.seattlecenter.com/about/accessibility.aspx

If you are coming by Light Rail it is best to get off at Westlake Station and then ride the Monorail over to the Seattle Center which drops you off right at the Armory.

***

Seattle Indies strives to be an inclusive and welcoming community for everyone. By attending our events, you are agreeing to follow our code of conduct (https://www.seattleindies.org/code-of-conduct/).

description:
Socrates Café meets twice a month. Though this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, morality, and the first principles of things.

Prior to each meeting we vote online for the questions we will discuss. That way, we will have enough time to ruminate on them and have more in-depth conversations. If you RSVP to a meeting, you may post your question in the event comments section below. I'll send ou
long_description:
Socrates Café meets twice a month. Though this may be considered a "philosophical" group, there are no rules as to what is discussed. Usually, the topics revolve around social concerns, morality, and the first principles of things.

Prior to each meeting we vote online for the questions we will discuss. That way, we will have enough time to ruminate on them and have more in-depth conversations. If you RSVP to a meeting, you may post your question in the event comments section below. I'll send out a survey for voting a few days prior to the meetup. We discuss two questions each night. So you will get to cast two votes in the survey.

When we meet, we break into smaller groups of five to seven to discuss the top two vote-getters. Each group discusses one question for around 45-50 minutes, and we then take a short break. After reconvening, each group moves on to its second question.

Hope to see you there!

-Brian

This small, family run restaurant features cuisine that is exotic, sophisticated and unique. Burma is the melting pot capitol of the world.
Their distinct blend of food reflects this.

Their food is similar to their neighbors but has it's own blend of ingredients and flavors.

Authentic Burmese home cooking.

They have been around for many years. Located in Stanton, a small town in north Orange County
.
Their dishes are prepared from scratch using raw ingredients and focusing on healthy, light dishes.

The MENU is amazing

Appetizers
include samusas which are like Indian samosas but different. Burmese falafels...Paratha as Myanmar borders India.

All the salads sound delicious. I still remember their signature tea leaf salad. Two other salads that strike me are the ginger salad and Burmese chicken salad.

Oodles of noodles such as coconut noodles, garlic noodles, and Burmese pad Thai.

And we cannot forget Burmese biryani rice dishes.
Burmese catfish chowder!!!!
Coconut chicken soup.
Beef curry noodle soup.
Mint leaf chicken.
Garlic butter shrimp.
Mango chicken.
Basil fish curry.
Multiple other curries!
Tea leaf lamb is a must try.
Pumpkin pork stew, how does that sound?

**www.eatburma.com**
**www.irrawaddytaste.com**

**Most people will be eating family style so we can try a bunch of their delicious dishes. A few members will order individually. This blend of dining options works well. No other foodie groups do this**
**.**
**Irrawaddy's food is based upon family recipes and Burmese street food.**
**Their signature dish is the tea leaf salad:**
**Romaine lettuce, fried garlic, fried mashed lentils, and pumpkin seeds. The special dressing is made from imported Burmese tea leaves.**

**https://eatburma. com**
**www.irrawaddytaste.com**

**yelp 4.7 stars with 798 reviews**
**4.7 on google**
**ex-pats on yelp love the authentic food**

**the only Burmese restaurant in OC

Class Description:
Curious about meditation but not sure where to begin? This class is a friendly introduction to the yogic approach to meditation—beyond “clearing your mind” or sitting perfectly still. We’ll explore what meditation is, why it matters, and how to practice in a way that feels accessible and meaningful.

You’ll be guided through simple, grounding practices including **mantra meditation**, **japa (repetition)**, and an introduction to **kirtan (call-and-response chanting)**. We’ll also weave in light yoga philosophy to give context—so you understand the purpose behind the practice, not just the technique.

No experience necessary. Come as you are—curious, open, or even skeptical. This is a space to learn, ask questions, and build a practice you can actually take home.

long_description:
The glorious India Tour will prove to be the most beautiful vacation of your life. Fall in love with the incredible diversity of culture, art, expression, history, cuisines, and traditions. Visit the most iconic states of the country during the tour. Sample the Indian cuisine, but make sure that you don’t get the infamous Delhi Belly. Admire the enchanting beauty of the Taj Mahal and visit the innumerable palaces and forts. Shop to your heart’s content at the local markets and enjoy the unique experiences of camel and elephant safari. Go boating at the backwaters of Kerala, and indulge in partying and revelry at Goa. Soak in the serene ambiance of Munnar and return home safe with hordes of photos, travel memories, and souvenirs from India.

long_description:
Join the Leh-Ladakh adventure on this trip to India. This trip will make you fall in love with Ladakh with your visit to the land of an incredible blend of mountains, forests, deserts, lakes, rivers, waterfalls, and more in just a week.
Leh Ladakh resembles Tibet in terms of topography and culture and you wouldn’t want to miss its barren lands, High Mountain passes, and unique customs.
Located in the Indian state of Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh is one of the most popular tourist destinations in India. The region is known for its breathtaking scenery, snow-capped mountains, clean ice lakes, and winding roads. The ancient Buddhist monasteries, largely tucked in the mountains and dating back thousands of years, add to its outstanding beauty.
The journey to one of the most magnificent and dynamic landscapes on the planet, with most of the world’s highest motor-able crossings and the breathtaking splendor of snow-capped mountains, provides you with once in a lifetime experience.

Highlights

Visited Places:

* Delhi
* Leh
* Shanti Stupa, Leh Market, and Leh Palace
* Gurudwara Pathar Sahib
* Indus valley and Zanskar
* Nubra Valley via Khardung La pass
* Diskit monastery
* Pangong Tso Lake
* Thiksey monastery and Shey Palace

Travel Experience:

* A unique fusion of culture and nature with the best experience
* Explore the stunning looking Himalayan peaks
* Explore Diskit monastery, some marvelous lakes like Pangong Tso Lake and Khardung La pass
* Relish the amazing Camel ride and lovely Hundar Valley

long_description:
**GO TO EVENTBRITE FOR LINK TO MEETING:**
Recovering from Religion EUROPE BASED WOMEN'S VIRTUAL Support Group Tickets\, Multiple Dates \| Eventbrite

This is an RfR-wide event, not tied to any particular local chapter.

\*NOTE: This meeting is solely for individuals who identify as female, non-binary and gender-fluid.

The Recovering from Religion WOMEN'S chapter support group [Europe-based time zones] will meet the 2nd Tuesday of each month @ 6pm local time UK, unless the date falls on a holiday. Attendees are welcome to share, and may also decide to remain anonymous if they so choose.

The primary focus of a Recovering From Religion support group is to provide ongoing and personal support to individuals as they let go of their religious beliefs. This transitional period is an ongoing process that can result in a range of emotions, as well as a ripple effect of consequences throughout an individual’s life. As such, the support meetings are safe and anonymous places to express these doubts, fears, and experiences without biased feedback or proselytizing.

We are here to help each other through this journey.

There is no cost to attend this support group but, if you feel so inclined, donations can be made at www.recoveringfromreligion.org/donate

If you find you need to talk with someone before the next support meeting, RfR has a hotline and online chat for that express purpose. Go to www.recoveringfromreligion.org and click on the green chat bubble in the lower left corner of the site to chat online.

If you are in need of professional help, we can offer the Secular Therapy Project to provide options to connect with a professional therapist. All therapists have been thoroughly vetted by our organization and offer only evidence-based and non-religious treatment. Connect with them at www.seculartherapy.org.

Like what RfR does? Why not volunteer! There are quite a few options. Head over to www.recoveringfromreligion.org/volunteer for more info.

title: Demystifying JVM Garbage Collection
description:
Most of us don’t want to go back to the days of `malloc` and `free`. However, the magic of garbage collectors—while convenient—can often feel mysterious and difficult to understand.
In this talk, you’ll learn about the many different garbage collectors available in JVMs, along with the strengths and weaknesses of the allocation and collection strategies used by each. We’ll also explore how garbage collectors continue to evolve to support modern hardware and cloud environments.
The session will c
organizer: Boston Java Users ACM Chapter (formerly NEJUG)
long_description:
Most of us don’t want to go back to the days of `malloc` and `free`. However, the magic of garbage collectors—while convenient—can often feel mysterious and difficult to understand.
In this talk, you’ll learn about the many different garbage collectors available in JVMs, along with the strengths and weaknesses of the allocation and collection strategies used by each. We’ll also explore how garbage collectors continue to evolve to support modern hardware and cloud environments.
The session will cover core garbage collection concepts such as object reachability, concurrent collectors, parallel garbage collectors, and generational garbage collectors. These ideas will be explored by following the progression and evolution of garbage collectors in the HotSpot JVM.

Speaker:
[Douglas Hawkins](https://www.linkedin.com/in/dougqh/) has been passionately developing software for over **20 years**.
Throughout his career, Doug has focused on building **high-performance Java applications**, with experience spanning domains from **bioinformatics** to **financial exchanges**.
After a decade as a Java developer, Doug transitioned to working on the **Java Virtual Machine at Azul Systems**, deepening his expertise in JVM internals and performance engineering.
Today, Doug continues his work on performance tooling for developers as part of **Datadog’s Java Application Performance Monitoring team**.
While Doug remains passionate about developing software, his **true passion is sharing knowledge**—especially helping others understand **low-level JVM details and performance tuning**.
**Presentations**

long_description:
In-Person Documentary Night is usually held on every 2nd Friday of the month. This event was designed to give people the chance to discuss interesting ideas and topics explored in the documentaries that we have chosen as a group to watch. This month we voted to watch the the documentary, **Daughters of Dolma.** This film takes viewers on a journey revealing a distinctively female experience of Tibetan Buddhism in the Kathmandu Valley. **[>>Click here to watch the film trailer<<](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rFBsNOTXEIg)**

**We will start the film PROMPTLY AT 7:10 PM.**

For the event we will meet together in the sanctuary at Northwest Unitarian Universalist Congregation, where we will watch the film together. Then we will participate in multiple rounds of small group discussions with a different groups for each round. This gives you the opportunity to meet new people and hear a variety of perspectives throughout the night. We will end by deciding what to watch next month. **This is a Voting Night where we brainstorm and decide as a group what we will watch the following month, so please come with a recommendation ready!**

**Feel free to bring your dinner! Decaf and caffeinated tea will be provided. We will also be having potluck style snacks!** So you are welcome to bring food to share with others, whether homemade or store-bought. Please bring foods that won't be distracting for others during the film or the discussion. long_description:
Are you seeking community with other like-minded women?
A space where you can be yourself, grow and become the best of yourself?

Perhaps you have desired a sisterhood where personal growth, spiritual development and empowerment is the golden thread that brings them together. Then, if that is true for you, check us out!
Welcome to the Sacred Sisterhood – CSLDallas Women’s Circle. Here, we embrace women from all walks of life, stages, ages, races, cultures, and religious traditions. We are seekers, heart-centered, and yearning for something more.
Since ancient times, women have gathered in circles to share stories, celebrate, support each other, and forge bonds with their sisters, embodying our Oneness with Life and each other.

In this sacred space, our purpose is to love and transform ourselves while also transforming the world through connections and nourishing friendships. Through deep listening and understanding, we create an opportunity for growth in a spirit of equality and acceptance. When we feel seen, heard, and held, we can transcend current conditions and embrace our true radiance and power as magic happens.
Join us each month as we journey together towards love, transformation, and in a sisterhood of unity.
What you can expect from the group:

* Utilizing monthly themes, we will explore topics important to women through dialogue, active listening, journaling and spiritual principles and practices, grounded in the Science of Mind.
* From honoring our roles in the world – daughter, sister, mother, grandmother, aunt, and friend – we will share wisdom as well as stories of how women are the nurturers, gatherers and leaders working to transform our world. How can we make a difference?
* Celebrations, rituals, and gatherings – We will ‘lunch’ together once a quarter

When we meet:
We meet the 2nd Saturday of each month from 10am to noon in person at CSLDallas. In coming months, we may add or alternate with a virtual meeting.

long_description:
**with Madhurranjan Mohaan**
**accompanied by Krishna Parathasarathy, Violin, and Rahul Zingde, Tabla**

Join us for an evening of Hindustani Classical music!
Hindustani classical music, with its various ragas and melodies, can bring states of calm and relaxation, along with joyous intensity. The experience is likened by some to states attained during meditation.
The program features Madhyam pradhan Ragas.

Madhurranjan will present multiple ragas that don't have pancham and/or where madhyam is important.

He will be accompanied by Krishna Parathasarathy, Violin, and Rahul Zingde, Tabla.

**The emotions that are experienced during a Hindustani concert are not easily matched by any other forms of music.**

**Presented ONLY at 2929 24th Street, not online!**
This concert is open to all at no cost. We are supported by your generosity (dana). Donations are accepted and no one is ever turned away for lack of funds.

**Madhurranjan Mohaan (vocals)** is an engineer by morning and an aspiring musician after that. He tries to be a good human being most of the time though. Madhurranjan runs a non profit classical organization called Sangeethaamsha ([https://www.sangeethaamsha.com/)](https://www.sangeethaamsha.com/)) to spread the magic of classical music and an Indian classical based fusion band Bayraagis (@BayRaagis) to again spread the magic of classical music. Madhurranjan was initiated into Hindustani classical music at the age of 6 by his uncle, late Flute master B.N Suresh ji. He trained for about 7 years before taking a break. He has continued to learn Hindustani music for the last 8 years under the tutelage of Mewati Gharana guru Smt Lalita Sharma, a renowned disciple of Pt Jasraj ji.

title: TiE Young Entrepreneurs (TYE) Global Pitch Competition 2026
description: High school students from 32 global TYE chapters pitch their startups for seed funding and mentorship at TiE's flagship youth competition.
long_description: TiE Young Entrepreneurs (TYE) is an 8-week entrepreneurship program for high school students that culminates in a global pitch competition every June. Students from 32 chapters worldwide — including Silicon Valley, Seattle, Boston, Houston, and Dallas — present their startups to panels of investors and entrepreneurs. Winners receive seed funding, mentorship, and connections to TiE's global network. The program has produced over 20,000 alumni and countless real startups.
venue_info: Regional finals are held at local TiE chapters (Cambridge Innovation Center for Boston, TiE offices in Santa Clara for Silicon Valley). Global finals are typically virtual with an in-person component in the Bay Area.

long_description:
Pilot Project Brewing is located on Milwaukee Ave between the Western and California blue line stops. Parking is available on Milwaukee and nearby side streets.

Ask for Simon if you're having trouble finding us! No agenda or anything organized. Feel free to come early, get some work done at the tables reserved, get some brews and meet up with fellow Indie Hackers.

Non-alcoholic beverages will be available. They also have food for purchase. No outside food please.

We'll be implementing the [Pacman Rule](https://www.ericholscher.com/blog/2017/aug/2/pacman-rule-conferences/) at this meetup:

"When standing as a group of people, always leave room for 1 person to join your group. More memorably, stand like Pac-Man!

The new person, who has been given permission to join your group, will gather up the courage, and join you! Another important point, the group should now readjust to leave another space for a new person.

Leaving room for new people when standing in a group is a physical way to show an inclusive and welcoming environment. It reduces the feeling of there being cliques, and allows people to integrate themselves into the community."

New to Indie Hackers? Learn more here: https://www.indiehackers.com/start

Want to stay in touch? Check out our discord server:
[https://discord.gg/sbymDbfthq](https://discord.gg/sbymDbfthq)

long_description:
Volunteers of all cultures are welcome. Help cook and share a meal with Native American seniors at St. Kateri Center. We will cook both cultural relevant food for Indians (maze, beans, squash, wild rice, bison, fry bread, etc.) and popular American lunch items. Volunteers will also get to sit down and eat with the elders, and share conversations to learn about the Indian culture.

This is a recurring event on the third Thursday of every month.

Both experienced and non experienced volunteers are welcome. All cooking and plating instructions will be provided on site and it is easy. All volunteers must be 14 years or older. Minors must get their parents' or legal guardians' permission to participate.

Volunteers will meet at St. Kateri Center, next to St. Benedict Church

3938 N Leavitt St, Chicago, IL 60618

We will start cooking at 9 am and be ready to serve by noon. We will cook 40 to 80 meals to serve on site and pack some meals for home delivery. Volunteers will meet in the kitchen. The shift time is flexible. If you have to come later or leave early, that's OK.

Please dress appropriately to work in a kitchen. Wear closed toe shoes with non slip bottoms, like sneakers. Slacks, jeans or long pants. No shorts or tank tops allowed. You will be asked to wear a hair net or you can bring a baseball cap or hat to manage your hair. You can also bring your own apron if you own one.

There is free street parking in the area, usually on the same street or the next block. It is also near CTA bus routes.

St. Kateri Center of Chicago is a Ministry of St. Benedict Parish serving the community of American Indian Catholics through faith formation and traditional prayers.

long_description:
## **Urban Reset La Dera Park: Walking Meditation & Movement**

**Hosted by Monique Marie \| The Free Spirit Yogi**

### **From "Doing" into "Being"**

In the heart of the city lies a pocket of peace. Join us at **Ladera Park** for an intimate, guided journey designed to help you shed the noise of the week and return to your center. This isn't just a yoga class; it’s a curated experience of stillness, nature, and community.

### **The Experience**

Our reset is divided into four intentional phases:

* **The Silent Walk (40 Minutes):** We begin at our meeting spot with a single chime of the singing bowl. You will receive a **Mindful Focus Card**—a tactile, hand-held guide to anchor your thoughts as you wander toward the oaks. Every few minutes, the chime will ring again, calling you to take one deep, conscious breath, notice exactly where you are, and continue your journey in silence.
* **The Movement (35 Minutes):** Once we reach the dappled shade of the oak grove, we transition from the internal journey to the physical. We will move through a grounding yoga flow designed to integrate the peace of your walk into your body.
* **The Integration (5 Minutes):** We conclude our journey by bringing the stillness of the park into the center of our being. As we settle into our final resting pose, the "doing" is officially done. This is your time to absorb the frequency of the trees, the rhythm of your breath, and the shift in your energy.
* The play. Lets challenge our balance by trying arm balances, inversions and new asanas to deepen our practice.
* The departure. One final collective breath to share gratitude.

### **What’s Provided**

To ensure you can remain fully "hands-free" and present, we provide:

* **Yoga Mat Backpacks:** To ensure you can fully immerse yourself in the walking meditation, we provide complimentary use of our Yoga Mat Backpacks for the duration of the experience.
* **Mindful Focus Cards:** Yours to use during the event.

description:
**THE BOOK**
Heart Lamp: Selected Stories
In the twelve stories of Heart Lamp, Banu Mushtaq exquisitely captures the everyday lives of women and girls in Muslim communities in southern India. Published originally in the Kannada language between 1990 and 2023, praised for their dry and gentle humour, these portraits of family and community tensions testify to Mushtaq’s years as a journalist and lawyer, in which she tirelessly championed women’s rights and protested all forms of caste and religiou
long_description:
**THE BOOK**
Heart Lamp: Selected Stories
In the twelve stories of Heart Lamp, Banu Mushtaq exquisitely captures the everyday lives of women and girls in Muslim communities in southern India. Published originally in the Kannada language between 1990 and 2023, praised for their dry and gentle humour, these portraits of family and community tensions testify to Mushtaq’s years as a journalist and lawyer, in which she tirelessly championed women’s rights and protested all forms of caste and religious oppression. Written in a style at once witty, vivid, colloquial, moving and excoriating, it’s in her characters – the sparky children, the audacious grandmothers, the buffoonish maulvis and thug brothers, the oft-hapless husbands, and the mothers above all, surviving their feelings at great cost – that Mushtaq emerges as an astonishing writer and observer of human nature, building disconcerting emotional heights out of a rich spoken style. Her opus has garnered both censure from conservative quarters as well India’s most prestigious literary awards; this is a collection sure to be read for years to come.

**THE AUTHOR**
Banu Mushtaq (ಬಾನು ಮುಷ್ತಾಕ್, born 1948) is an activist, lawyer and writer from the southern Indian state of Karnataka. She writes in the Kannada language and her works have also been published in Urdu, Hindi, Tamil, Malayalam and, most recently, English.

title: Baltimore Running Festival Marathon 2026
description: Boston Marathon qualifying race through Baltimore's neighborhoods, finishing at the iconic Inner Harbor. Multiple distances from 5K to marathon.
long_description: The Baltimore Running Festival offers five race distances through Charm City's most scenic neighborhoods. The marathon is a certified Boston Marathon qualifier with a challenging but rewarding course. Runners pass through Federal Hill, Fells Point, Canton, and along the waterfront before finishing at the Inner Harbor. The festival atmosphere, with live bands and enthusiastic crowds, makes it one of the Mid-Atlantic's best fall races.
venue_info: Start/finish at McKeldin Plaza, Inner Harbor. Course passes through Federal Hill, Fells Point, and Canton. The Light Rail and bus service reach the Inner Harbor area. Under Armour finisher shirt included with registration.

title: Dussehra & Ramlila — BAPS Akshardham, Robbinsville NJ
description: Dussehra celebrations at the world's largest Hindu temple outside India, featuring Ramlila and cultural programs.
long_description: Celebrate Dussehra (Vijayadashami) at the spectacular BAPS Akshardham in Robbinsville, the largest Hindu temple in the Western hemisphere. The evening program includes a Ramlila dramatization of Lord Rama's victory over Ravana, followed by the symbolic burning of Ravana's effigy. Cultural performances, fireworks, and prasadam round out the festivities.
venue_info: 112 N Main St, Robbinsville, NJ 08691. Free parking. Weekend registration required for Akshardham Campus. Closed Tuesdays. Wheelchair accessible.

title: Project Samskriti: Indian Classical Arts Tour – San Francisco
description: Isha Foundation's Project Samskriti comes to the Bay Area — Bharatanatyam, Carnatic music, and Kalaripayattu performances and workshops at Cañada College in Redwood City. A rare opportunity to experience India's classical performing arts tradition.

title: Nashville Half Marathon, Marathon & 5K 2026
description: Music City's signature fall running event with half marathon, full marathon, and 5K options. A Boston Marathon qualifier with a finish festival.
long_description: The Nashville Marathon and Half Marathon is Music City's premier fall running event and a certified Boston Marathon qualifier. The course winds through Nashville's vibrant neighborhoods, passing iconic landmarks and live music stages along the way. The 2026 edition features a half marathon, full marathon, and 5K, with a festive finish at First Horizon Park complete with live music, food, and a celebratory atmosphere.
venue_info: First Horizon Park (Nashville Sounds baseball stadium), 19 Junior Gilliam Way. The 5K starts at 7:00 AM, marathon at 7:00 AM. Free race shirts and medals for finishers. Parking available near the stadium.

title: Marine Corps Marathon 2026 — The People's Marathon
description: The third-largest US marathon and world's largest with no prize money. Run past DC's monuments with Marines cheering you on.
long_description: Known as 'The People's Marathon,' the Marine Corps Marathon is the third-largest marathon in the US and the world's largest without prize money. The 51st edition takes runners on a spectacular tour of Washington DC — past the Pentagon, along the Potomac, through Georgetown, around the National Mall, and past the Capitol. US Marines manage every mile, handing out hydration, cheering runners on, and placing finisher medals. The emotional 'wear blue: run to remember' mile honors fallen service members. Registration opens April 6.
venue_info: Start: Pentagon parking lot, Arlington, VA. Finish: Marine Corps War Memorial (Iwo Jima). Metro (Pentagon station, Blue/Yellow lines) is the best way to get there. Health & Fitness Expo at the National Building Museum. 6-hour time limit.

title: Project Samskriti: Indian Classical Arts Tour – Seattle
description: Isha Foundation's Project Samskriti brings Indian classical arts to Seattle — Bharatanatyam, Carnatic music, and Kalaripayattu (oldest martial art in the world). Extended 9-day residency with workshops and performances at Broadway Performance Hall.

title: TCS New York City Marathon 2026
description: The world's largest marathon with 60,000+ runners through all five NYC boroughs. A bucket-list race celebrating its 50th anniversary course.
long_description: The TCS New York City Marathon is the world's largest marathon and one of the six World Marathon Majors. Over 60,000 runners from 130+ countries cross the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge and run through all five boroughs — Staten Island, Brooklyn, Queens, the Bronx, and Manhattan — before the iconic Central Park finish. The 2026 edition marks the 50th anniversary of the five-borough course. Two million spectators line the streets, making it arguably the most electrifying marathon atmosphere on Earth. The race has raised over $600 million for charity since 2006.
venue_info: Start: Fort Wadsworth, Staten Island (ferry/bus transport from Manhattan). Finish: Central Park, near Tavern on the Green. Subway serves the finish area (B/C to 72nd St). Entry is by lottery, charity, or guaranteed qualifier. 59,226 finishers in 2025.

long_description: Experience Diwali at the magnificent BAPS Akshardham in Robbinsville, NJ — the largest Hindu temple in the Western hemisphere. The campus transforms with thousands of lights, rangoli, and diyas. Features devotional programs, cultural performances, fireworks, and a community dinner. An awe-inspiring setting for the Festival of Lights.
venue_info: 112 N Main St, Robbinsville, NJ. Massive parking facility. Free registration required for weekend visits. Campus closed Tuesdays. Modest dress code required.
